title: VM waitable reserve and cold file-backed prefault
summary: Convert ReserveUserRangeOp from a one-shot adapter into a waitable PageProgress StepOp, preserve RangeLock and file-page wait sources through syscall drivers, continue fault materialization after exact-source wake through a recipe-generation fast path, and add cold file-backed VMA regressions.

steps.title: Add monotonic recipe-generation fast and slow revalidation
steps.notes: Use an AtomicU64 even/odd publication sequence, bounded stamped lookup with no reader spin, no-wrap admission, one-word post-wake fast comparison, and the existing target-field slow path on mismatch or an unstamped observation. Keep local backing/page-index validation on both paths; never use a one-bit or root-pointer token.

steps.title: Make ReserveUserRangeOp waitable and publication-safe
steps.notes: TDD: first pin file-fetch Yield, RangeLock Yield, retry completion, PageProgress, and terminal EFAULT; then remove OneShotStepOp, retain only an owned stamped VmFaultOutcome across Yield, and route publish through fresh RangeLock plus generation revalidation.

steps.title: Drive async prefaults and make writev hot path fall through
steps.notes: Buffered read/write and O_DIRECT use drive Waiting. The synchronous writev optimization claims only hot user PTEs and returns None for cold inputs or pre-progress destination Yield so dispatch_full_syscall falls back to async writev.

steps.title: Wait on the exact fault token source
steps.notes: RangeLock waits retain their owned endpoint fast path; file/backend tokens resolve their exact registered source id. Unknown ids fail closed and never substitute RangeLock. After wake the inner loop retries materialization from the owned stamped outcome; generation mismatch takes full target revalidation, and only incompatible target change restarts recipe resolution.

steps.title: Run VM and step gates and catch up progress
steps.notes: Mark the plan complete only after all focused gates pass or inherited unrelated failures are recorded precisely. The research note records why buffered copy is not a generic zero-copy candidate.

risks: A cursor must advance only after an adequate PTE exists or publication commits; advancing before Yield would skip the blocked page.
A one-bit dirty/toggle stamp or a root-pointer token is ABA-unsafe; the sequence must be a monotonic full word and must fail before wrap.
The recipe sequence must become odd before the root swap and publish the next even value after it; changing this ordering can pair a stale recipe with a falsely current stamp.
A reader that overlaps an odd or changing sequence must retain an unstamped owned outcome and force slow revalidation; it must not spin unboundedly inside StepOp::step.
Generation equality may skip only the recipe-tree lookup; backing kind and materialization page index still require local validation.
A global sequence mismatch may come from an unrelated VMA rewrite, so mismatch must enter the existing field-level slow path rather than force an outer-loop restart.
DriveMode::Nonblocking would expose EAGAIN for user-memory page faults; prefault drivers must use Waiting independently of file O_NONBLOCK.
The writev hot lane must not fall back after bytes were committed or it could duplicate writes; partial progress returns the byte count.
A materialized frame must be dropped if publication revalidation blocks or detects a stale recipe, releasing its MapPin safely.
Fault wait routing must cover substrate WaitSource and registered raw-wire sources without waiting on an unrelated carrier.
blockers: Before implementation claims a write set, coordinate with or close the active docs/progress/plans/2026-05-26-ltp-network-remaining-blockers.json claims over crates/tx-subsystems/src/vm, crates/tx-shims/src/linux_syscall/mod.rs, and docs/progress/STATUS.md.
